name: title_block_says_what_it_wants
why: ENTRY GT3. A title block does not contain text: it contains LINKS to custom properties, written `$PRP:"Nome"`. Filling it means writing those properties -- and `set_property` already knew how. The half was missing that the entry itself called two hours of work by hand: **reading which variables the title block really references, because they cannot be guessed.**
defect_caught: The name of the property written with a different spelling from the one the title block references -- a capital letter, a space, the language -- **gives no error**: SOLIDWORKS writes the property, the title block does not show it, and the PDF comes out with the box empty. It is the third case of the same family in two days: `40x40x3` against `40X40X3` on the profiles, `.sldprt` against `.SLDPRT` on the paths, and now the name of a property. **Same name, two spellings, no error.**
_what_the_probe_said_about_this_shops_ti: Measured on 18/9/2026 on the drawing template of this workshop (`Disegno.drwdot`): 39 notes, seven of them linked. It asks for TRATTAMENTO, REVISIONE, CREAZIONE_DATA (capitals), Descrizione, Materiale, Peso, MASSA. **The spelling is mixed inside the same title block**, and there is no rule: there is what somebody wrote when they made it. That is why the list is asked for instead of deduced.
_and_almost_all_of_them_are_PRPSHEET: That is, they must be written on the PART, not on the drawing: `$PRPSHEET` takes the property from the model shown in the view. Writing them on the drawing would leave them all empty, and nobody would say anything. That is why the operation marks those entries with «(from the part, not from the drawing)» instead of just listing them.
_and_the_TitleBlock_is_missing: `ISheet.get_TitleBlock()` returns null on this drawing template: the title block is made of notes of the FORMAT, not of a real title block. The operation tries both roads and says which one answered -- had it tried only the first, it would have said «no title block» on a drawing that has one.

expect.why: the part the drawing is made on

**IT IS WRITTEN ON THE PART, not on the drawing**, and the case does it before creating the drawing on purpose: the title block asks for it with `$PRPSHEET`, that is from the model shown in the view. Written on the drawing it would stay empty in the title block, and neither of the two sides would say anything.
`Add3` answers a code, not the value: the operation RE-READS after writing, and this field is the one it re-read -- not the one it passed
a view attaches to the path of the part
the bench follows the new document (entry GT0)

steps._and_the_part_is_named_explicitly: **ON 18/9/2026 THIS LINE WAS NOT THERE, AND THE DRAWING CAME OUT OF THE WRONG PART.** Without «model», `standard_views` fell back on the FIRST document open — an order nobody declares — and the part of the other drawing case, still open, came first. Three views, no error, and the title block that read the `$PRPSHEET` from a part that had nothing to do with it. Now the operation refuses instead of drawing lots, and the case says which part it wants instead of hoping there is only one.

expect.why: `$PRPSHEET` takes the property from the model **shown in a view**: without views the title block would not know which part to read from

**THE PART THAT MAKES THE ENTRY WORTH IT.** They are the EXACT names this title block references, with their spelling -- `TRATTAMENTO` in capitals and `Descrizione` capitalised, inside the same title block. The model copies them instead of guessing them, and the category of error disappears.

**FIRST OF ALL: COULD I LOOK?** If the operation cannot reach the model referenced by the view, the two lists below are empty out of ignorance and not by measurement — and a list empty out of ignorance passes any `non_contiene`. Here we demand the PATH of the part, so «I found nothing» and «I could not look» remain two different answers.

**IT COMES BEFORE THE EXPECTATION THAT EXPLAINS, AND IT MUST.** The bench stops the case at the FIRST red expectation (`DeclaredCases.cs`, `if (!ok) return false`): a diagnostic line put AFTER the one that fails is never executed — built on 18/9/2026 and put at the tail, it did not speak. *A witness put in line behind the defendant does not testify.* Here it says which of the two faults it is: if this one is red, the property IS on the model and the link did not resolve it (and rewriting it is no use); if it is green and the next one is red, the property did not reach the model.

**THE CIRCLE CLOSES HERE, and it is a positive assertion, not the absence of a fault.** The property was written on the PART at step 2; the title block of the DRAWING shows it now. Two different documents, and the `$PRPSHEET` link that joins them really worked. «It is not in the list of the empty ones» would not have proved the same thing: not being among the broken ones is not working.

THE RED CASE THAT LIVES IN THE SAME RUN. `Materiale` is asked for by the title block and nobody wrote it: it must be listed among the empty ones. If this list were empty, the expectation above would prove nothing -- it would only prove that the operation always says «everything shown».

on this drawing template `get_TitleBlock()` returns null, and the notes are in the FORMAT of the sheet. The operation tries both roads and says which one answered: if one day the drawing template changed and a real title block were born, this expectation would turn red and say so, instead of letting the road change silently.
the warning travels with the answer, not only in the description of the operation: whoever reads this answer may never have read the catalogue
